items.title: 1.0: Current Studio
items.body: A privacy-first, local-first geospatial editor for journeys, tracks, POIs, Cesium 2D/3D scenes, camera controls, widgets, replay, snapshots, video, and PDF or HTML journey reports.

items.title: 1.1: Extended activity imports
items.body: Add FIT and TCX imports from Garmin and Strava while preserving activity and sensor data, with optional authenticated Strava access and connected-provider project files.

items.title: 1.2: Timeline video editor
items.body: Replace the separate Replay start, replay, and stop clip controls with a track-based timeline combining journey replay, clips, and widgets.

items.title: 1.3: 3D camera path editor
items.body: Create editable 3D camera paths with GPS positions, altitude, duration, motion profiles, look-at targets, easing, and optional 360-degree moves.

access.title: Studio is free to use.
access.note: Studio was designed so you can share your adventures as enriched videos without paying anything. Studio is and will remain completely free to use. During the trial period, Cesium access is shared and may have some limitations. After the trial, a completely free Cesium Ion account is needed to use your own Cesium resources or access additional basemaps. Paid basemaps are supported, but they are never required.

cards.title: Free Studio access
cards.body: Open Studio, edit journeys, and export outputs without a paid subscription. By default, Studio uses free GIS layers. You can also choose freemium or paid layers, but using them is never mandatory.

cards.title: Free Cesium access
cards.body: During the trial period, Studio provides shared Cesium access with limitations. After the trial, create a free Cesium Ion account to use your own resources, Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles, and Google or Azure basemaps.

cards.title: Technical relationship only
cards.body:
LGS1920 has no commercial relationship with Cesium or the GIS layer providers. Cesium is an open-source 3D globe engine.
Studio uses it solely to render the scene and its optional layers.

faq.title: Common questions about Studio and the public site.

items.summary: Why LGS1920? What does it mean?
items.body: LGS1920 stands for La Grande Sure, a 1,920-metre summit in the Chartreuse massif, in the French Alps, at GPS coordinates 45°20′07″ N, 5°42′11″ E (45.3353, 5.7031).
items.bodyAfter: It is a mountain that means a great deal to me: it is part of my family roots, and I was barely twelve when I climbed it for the first time with my family. At the time, it was my Mont Blanc — better still, my Everest.
items.bodyFinal: One of Studio’s journey samples is, appropriately, named LGS1920. It is one of my favourite hikes, and I still hike it once a year, 54 years later.
